vulnerability.title: Django MultiPartParser IE_sanitize strips only Windows backslash paths, allowing directory traversal through uploaded file names handed to upload handlers
vulnerability.category_l2: directory traversal via crafted multipart upload file names (unix absolute paths and dot segments)

critical_operation.description: IE_sanitize only truncates a file name at the last backslash, i.e. it strips Windows-style full paths. Unix-style absolute names ('/tmp/hax0rd.txt'), forward-slash descendants ('subdir/x') and dot segments ('../../x'), including forms produced by HTML entities before the html.unescape() call at the use site, pass through unchanged. MultiPartParser.parse applies this helper to the Content-Disposition filename and then hands the result to every upload handler via handler.new_file(field_name, file_name, ...). Built-in memory/temporary-file handlers ignore the name, but a custom upload handler that uses file_name to build a storage path can be traversed outside its upload directory. The fix replaces IE_sanitize with sanitize_file_name(), which performs html.unescape, keeps the Windows backslash cleanup, and additionally applies os.path.basename, removing unix absolute paths, forward-slash descendants and leading dot segments; IE_sanitize is kept as an alias.

entry_point.description: parse() drives the multipart boundary parser and processes each FILE part's Content-Disposition filename before calling the upload handlers.

trace.description: the Content-Disposition filename is read and decoded
the name is HTML-unescaped and passed through IE_sanitize, which strips only backslash-prefixed Windows paths
the surviving name is handed to each upload handler as file_name

location.verification_method: Static read of multipartparser.py at 3.0.2, 3.0.13, 3.0.14, 2.2.19 and 2.2.20, of the 3.0.x/2.2.x fix and test diffs and of the 3.0.14 release notes; git blob identity and tag ancestry were checked against a local clone. No upload was performed and no test suite run.

families: upstream git history and release tags
source_crosscheck.notes: The Django announcement, NVD, OSV/GHSA and the fixed tags agree on the three ranges (2.2 <2.2.20, 3.0 <3.0.14, 3.1 <3.1.8) and on the IE_sanitize root cause. NVD assigns CWE-22 and CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM; GHSA labels the issue MODERATE with the same vector; the Django advisory labels it low. The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS). OSV's GIT introduced events again name unrelated security-archive documentation commits, and the fixed events are the 2.2.20/3.0.14/3.1.8 release commit, so fix verification used the five vendor-listed changesets and git ancestry instead.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read MultiPartParser.IE_sanitize and its call site at 3.0.2 and confirm that only backslash-prefixed paths are stripped.
An independent reviewer must confirm e7fba622 is absent from 3.0.2 and 3.0.13 and an ancestor of 3.0.14, and that 3.0.14 uses sanitize_file_name with os.path.basename.
An independent reviewer must confirm the 3.1.8 and 2.2.20 fixes and the three release boundaries against a second source family.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No multipart upload was sent and no Django test suite was executed; the finding is static.
The advisory states that built-in upload handlers were not affected; impact depends on a custom upload handler using file_name for path construction, and the specific handler was not surveyed.
The MITRE CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS).
NVD also carries a CVSS 2.0 metric of 5.0 (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N); the canonical score follows the NVD primary CVSS 3.1 metric.
The Django advisory's qualitative severity is low while NVD rates 5.3 MEDIUM and GHSA labels the issue MODERATE; the qualitative labels are recorded as source disagreement, not reconciled.
OSV's GIT range events are conversion artifacts: introduced events are later documentation commits and fixed events are the release commits; they were not used as fix evidence.

The fix leaves name components that are not absolute and contain no slash unchanged (os.path.basename of 'subdir/x' is 'x'; of '../../x' is 'x'), so the sanitizer is name-based and does not itself reject an upload; no residual weakness beyond that intended normalisation is claimed.
No downstream distribution backport (Debian, Fedora, SUSE, NetApp) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.
The snapshot inventory status is NEEDS_REVIEW with 67 ambiguous files, not a clean PASS.
open_questions: Which custom upload handlers in the wild build storage paths from the supplied file_name was not surveyed.
Whether any built-in handler in the 3.0.2 tree indirectly uses file_name for disk paths was checked only by reading the handler classes, not exercised.
